raw_response:
I am keeping chili on all 2.6 mu this year. I have done this for many years, and on such a small piece of land I cannot risk changing to something I do not know well. I do not read fertilizer numbers like technicians do, I look at the soil, the seedlings, and what worked before. Chili likes steady care. If I save too much on fertilizer or water, the plants stay weak and the peppers come small. But if I spend too much early, then I have no cash left if insects come later. So I will do it the usual way: plant after the weather turns warm and stable, use a moderate amount of base fertilizer, topdress a couple of times after the plants get going, and irrigate from the well when the soil turns dry. My land is small, so my family can handle most of the work ourselves. I would rather spend more labor than more cash.
